recipes.name: Bar / column chart
recipes.when: One number per category; compare sizes. Always start the value axis at 0.
steps: Band scale for categories on x, linear scale for values on y (0 at the bottom).
One rect per row: x = band(key), height = y(0) - y(value).
Gridlines and ticks come from the axis helpers; labels sit under each band.
recipes.combine: Add a second mark layer (target line, error bars) or sort rows to make it a ranking.

recipes.name: Grouped bar chart
recipes.when: Compare several series inside each category.
steps: Same band scale as a bar chart; each band is split into one slot per series.
Slot width = band width / number of series; offset = series index * slot width.
Colour = series (fixed order), never category.
recipes.combine: Swap to stacked when the total matters more than the individual parts.

recipes.name: Stacked bar chart
recipes.when: Totals matter and so do the parts that make them up.
steps: Keep a running baseline per category, starting at 0.
Each segment: top = y(base + v), height = y(base) - y(base + v); then base += v.
Domain must reach the largest total, not the largest segment.
recipes.combine: Only the bottom segment is easy to compare across bars. Use grouped if parts matter most.

recipes.name: 100% stacked bar
recipes.when: Compare composition (shares), not totals.
steps: Same as stacked, but divide each value by its category total first.
Fixed domain 0 to 1, tick labels formatted as percentages.
recipes.combine: Pair with a plain stacked chart if totals also matter.

recipes.name: Diverging stacked bar (Likert)
recipes.when: Survey scales: show agree vs disagree around a neutral centre.
steps: Linear x scale symmetric around 0 and wide enough for the longest side (neutral/2 + agree + strongly agree can exceed 80).
Negative side grows leftwards: half of neutral first, then disagree, then strongly disagree.
Positive side grows rightwards the same way. A heavy centre line marks 0.
recipes.combine: Sort rows by net agreement to turn it into a ranking.

recipes.name: Lollipop chart
recipes.when: Same job as a bar chart with less ink; good for many categories.
steps: Same scales as a bar chart.
Draw a thin line from the baseline to the value, then a circle on top.
recipes.combine: Highlight one category by changing only its circle colour.

recipes.name: Dumbbell chart
recipes.when: Before vs after (or two groups) for each item; the gap is the message.
steps: Band scale on y (one row per item), linear on x.
Connecting line first, then one circle per end so circles sit on top.
recipes.combine: Sort by gap size. Add arrowheads for direction of change.

recipes.name: Bullet chart
recipes.when: One value against a target, with qualitative ranges (poor / ok / good).
steps: Draw range bands widest first so narrower, darker bands overlay them.
Value bar is thinner than the band; target is a short vertical tick.
recipes.combine: Stack several in a column to make a compact KPI panel.

recipes.name: Radial bar chart
recipes.when: Decorative alternative to bars; inner rings are shorter, so read with care.
steps: Each category gets a concentric ring; value maps to an angle (here up to 270 degrees).
Ring shape comes from K.arc(cx, cy, innerR, outerR, startAngle, endAngle).
Labels go in the empty quarter where no ring reaches.
recipes.combine: Rarely worth combining; prefer a plain bar when accuracy matters.

recipes.name: Waterfall chart
recipes.when: How a starting value becomes an end value through gains and losses.
steps: Walk the rows keeping a running total: each bar spans from the old total to the new one.
Colour by sign; the final total bar starts at 0.
Thin connector lines link the end of one bar to the start of the next.
recipes.combine: Works as the bottom half of a P&L dashboard with a table beside it.

recipes.name: Marimekko (mosaic) chart
recipes.when: Two-way proportions: column width shows one share, segment height another.
steps: Column width = segment size (x scale 0..100); heights = shares within the column.
Track a running x offset for columns and a running base for segments.
recipes.combine: Annotate the largest cells; too many cells makes it unreadable.

recipes.name: Waffle chart
recipes.when: Shares of a whole that people should read as "out of 100".
steps: Turn each share into a count of cells out of 100 and build one colour per cell.
Cell i sits at column i % 10, row floor(i / 10); draw rows from the top.
recipes.combine: Replace squares with icons for a pictogram.

recipes.name: Funnel chart
recipes.when: Stages where each step loses some of the previous one.
steps: Half-width of each stage = value / max * a fixed maximum half-width, centred on one axis; labels go in a column on the right so narrow stages stay readable.
Between stage i and i+1 draw a trapezoid (polygon) joining their edges.
recipes.combine: Add conversion % between stages as small labels.

recipes.name: Pareto chart
recipes.when: Find the few causes that explain most of the total (the 80/20 view).
steps: Sort descending, convert to % of total, and draw bars.
Cumulative % line on the SAME 0..100% axis (no second axis needed).
recipes.combine: Bars + line is the classic two-layer combo; add a dashed 80% reference line.

recipes.name: Population pyramid
recipes.when: Two mirrored distributions over the same categories (age bands by sex, A vs B).
steps: Symmetric x scale around 0; the left series is drawn with negative width.
Bands on y, oldest at the top; centre line at 0; tick labels use absolute values.
recipes.combine: Use as a small multiple across years to show change.

recipes.name: Slope chart
recipes.when: How each item changed between exactly two moments.
steps: Two vertical axes (x = left and right); one shared y scale.
One line per item from (left, before) to (right, after); colour by direction of change.
recipes.combine: With many time points it becomes a line chart; with ranks only, a bump chart.

recipes.name: Histogram
recipes.when: Shape of ONE numeric variable: centre, spread, skew, gaps.
steps: Choose a range and a number of bins; K.hist counts values per bin.
x is a linear scale over the value range; bar height = count.
Bin count changes the story: try 10, 25 and 60 before trusting a shape.
recipes.combine: Layer a density curve and a rug on top (see Combining recipes).

recipes.name: Density plot (KDE)
recipes.when: A smooth version of the histogram; good for comparing several groups.
steps: Kernel density: put a small bell curve on every data point and add them up (K.kde).
Bandwidth sets smoothness; Silverman's rule (K.bw) is a sensible default.
Draw as a filled path closed along the baseline.
recipes.combine: Overlay several groups with transparency, or stack as a ridgeline.

recipes.name: Box plot
recipes.when: Compare spread, median and outliers across groups at a glance.
steps: Sort each group; get Q1, median, Q3 with K.quantile.
Whiskers reach the furthest points within 1.5 x IQR of the box; the rest are outliers.
Draw whisker line, box, median bar, then outlier dots.
recipes.combine: Overlay the raw points (jitter) so n and clusters are visible.

recipes.name: Violin plot
recipes.when: Box plot plus the full shape (bimodality shows up here, not in a box).
steps: Compute a KDE per group over the same y range.
Evaluate each KDE only between that group's own min and max so the tails do not become thin spikes.
Mirror it around the group centre: walk down the right edge, back up the left, close the path.
recipes.combine: Draw a narrow box plot inside the violin.

recipes.name: Ridgeline (joy) plot
recipes.when: Compare many distributions that would overlap on one axis.
steps: One KDE per group, each drawn on its own baseline spaced down the page.
Draw the top row first so lower rows overlap it; fill with the page background so overlaps hide cleanly.
recipes.combine: Order rows by median to show a trend across groups.

recipes.name: Beeswarm / strip plot
recipes.when: Show every point (small n) without overlap, plus the shape.
steps: Place points in sorted order along the value axis.
For each, try offsets 0, +r, -r, +2r, -2r... until it no longer touches an already placed point.
recipes.combine: Add a median tick, or colour points by a second variable.

recipes.name: ECDF (cumulative distribution)
recipes.when: Read percentiles directly; compare groups without choosing bins.
steps: Sort the data; the curve climbs 1/n at every observation.
Draw as steps: horizontal to the value, then up one notch.
recipes.combine: Overlay two groups; the vertical gap is the difference in percentiles.

recipes.name: Q-Q plot
recipes.when: Check whether data follow a normal distribution (or any reference).
steps: Standardise the sorted data to z-scores.
Pair each with the normal quantile at (i + 0.5) / n using K.invNorm.
Points on the diagonal mean normal; a curve means skew, a tilt in the tails means heavy tails.
recipes.combine: Place beside a histogram of the same data and the Shapiro-Wilk result.

recipes.name: Rug / barcode plot
recipes.when: Raw observation positions for several groups in minimal space.
steps: One thin vertical tick per observation along a shared value axis.
Semi-transparent ticks pile up into darker regions, which acts as a density cue.
recipes.combine: Usually drawn under a histogram or density curve as a second layer.

recipes.name: 2D density (binned heatmap)
recipes.when: Scatter plot with too many points; show where they pile up.
steps: Divide both axes into square bins and count points per bin.
Draw a rect per non-empty bin; opacity = count / max count.
recipes.combine: Hexagonal bins are the same idea with a different tile shape.

recipes.name: Layering: histogram + density + normal fit + rug
recipes.when: Several marks on ONE set of scales, each answering a different question.
steps: Pick one coordinate system (x value, y density) and make every layer use it.
Rescale the histogram to density (count / (n * binWidth)) so it matches the curves.
Draw back to front: bars, rug, KDE line, then the fitted normal as a dashed line.
recipes.combine: The same pattern gives scatter + regression line + confidence band, or bars + target line.

recipes.name: Layering: violin + box + jittered points
recipes.when: Shape, summary and raw data in one glance.
steps: Violin outline first (light), then a narrow box, then the points on top.
Jitter horizontally with a seeded random so the picture is reproducible.
recipes.combine: Same layering idea: any distribution plot can carry the raw points.

recipes.name: Small multiples (same chart, one panel per group)
recipes.when: Compare many groups without overplotting: repeat one chart with SHARED scales.
steps: Define the scales once, from the data of ALL groups, so panels are comparable.
Loop over groups; translate a <g> to each grid cell and call the same drawing code.
recipes.combine: Works for any chart type; this is how to compare 20 regions or 12 months.

recipes.name: Linked views: filter one chart, the other updates
recipes.when: Exploration: select a range in one chart and see what it means in another.
steps: Keep ONE shared state object (here: the selected x range).
Each chart is a function of (data, state); a single update() redraws all of them.
Controls only change state, then call update(); charts never talk to each other directly.
recipes.combine: Replace sliders with a drag-brush, or link a map and a table the same way.

recipes.name: Line chart
recipes.when: Change over time for a few series.
steps: Time (or index) on a linear x scale, value on y; the order of points matters.
One path per series: K.path joins the scaled points; round the line joins.
Direct labels at the line ends replace a legend.
recipes.combine: Add a shaded band (uncertainty), markers for events, or switch to small multiples when there are more than 4 series.

recipes.name: Area chart
recipes.when: Emphasise the magnitude (volume) of one series over time.
steps: Same scales as a line chart; the baseline must be 0 because the filled area encodes size.
Close the path along the baseline (L x(last) y(0) L x(0) y(0) Z), semi-transparent fill plus a solid top line.
recipes.combine: Stack several for composition, or overlay two with transparency.

recipes.name: Stacked area chart
recipes.when: Total and composition over time.
steps: Keep a cumulative array per x; band j runs from cum[j-1] to cum[j].
Each band is a polygon: forward along its upper edge, backward along its lower edge.
recipes.combine: Normalise to 100% to show shares; smooth the edges with K.curve for a streamgraph look.

recipes.name: Streamgraph
recipes.when: Many categories over time where the overall shape and rise or fall matter more than exact values.
steps: Stack like a stacked area, but start the baseline at -total/2 so the whole shape is centred.
Draw each layer's edges with K.curve (spline) for the flowing look.
recipes.combine: Best with direct labels on the thickest layers.

recipes.name: Step chart
recipes.when: Values that hold until they change (prices, settings, queue length).
steps: For each new value draw a horizontal run to its x, then a vertical jump to the new level.
Never interpolate between points: a straight line would claim values that never existed.
recipes.combine: Overlay events (vertical rules) that explain the jumps.

recipes.name: Sparklines
recipes.when: Tiny trends next to numbers in tables and dashboards.
steps: No axes, no gridlines: one thin line scaled to its own min and max.
Mark only the last point (dot) and print its value beside it.
recipes.combine: Put one in every row of a table (see "Table with sparklines" in the tables family).

recipes.name: Candlestick (OHLC) chart
recipes.when: Prices that have an open, high, low and close for every period.
steps: For each day: wick = line from low to high; body = rect from open to close.
Colour by direction (close above open = up). Body height uses Math.abs so it is never negative.
recipes.combine: Add a moving-average line and a volume bar chart in a panel below sharing the x scale.

recipes.name: Calendar heatmap
recipes.when: Daily activity patterns (weekday vs weekend, streaks, holidays).
steps: Columns = weeks, rows = weekday (0 to 6); cell = one day.
Colour comes from a sequential ramp K.seq(value / max); empty days stay pale.
Weeks use the day index: week = floor(i / 7), weekday = i % 7.
recipes.combine: Pair with a bar chart of weekly totals sharing the same week axis.

recipes.name: Gantt chart
recipes.when: A schedule: who or what happens when, and what depends on what.
steps: x = linear time scale; one row per task (band scale); bar from start to end.
Dependencies are elbow connectors from the end of one bar to the start of the next.
recipes.combine: Add a "today" line, progress fill inside bars, or colour by owner.

recipes.name: Timeline
recipes.when: A short list of dated events in order.
steps: One horizontal axis scaled by date; each event is a dot on the axis.
Alternate labels above and below with a stem so neighbours do not collide.
recipes.combine: Draw it above a line chart so events explain the bumps.

recipes.name: Fan chart (forecast with uncertainty)
recipes.when: Forecasts: show the best guess AND how fast certainty is lost.
steps: History is a normal line; the forecast starts at the last observation.
Uncertainty grows with horizon: band half-width = z * sigma * sqrt(h). Draw wide bands first, narrow on top.
recipes.combine: Overlay the actual values later to evaluate calibration.

recipes.name: Bump chart (rank over time)
recipes.when: Who leads, who falls: ranks matter, exact values do not.
steps: y = rank (1 at the top, so the scale runs 1 to n downwards).
One line with circles per series; labels at both ends so lines can be identified. Use straight segments: a spline would overshoot and suggest ranks that never existed.
recipes.combine: Highlight one series and grey out the rest.

recipes.name: Horizon chart
recipes.when: Many time series stacked in little vertical space.
steps: Slice the value range into bands (here 3). Each band is an area scaled to the full row height.
Draw the bands on top of each other with the same transparency: more layers = darker = larger value.
Positive values are blue, negative red, so one row shows both.
recipes.combine: Stack one row per region to compare many series at once.

recipes.name: Scatter plot
recipes.when: Relationship between two numeric variables; spot clusters and outliers.
steps: Two linear scales (do not force zero if the data sits far from it).
One semi-transparent circle per row so overlaps stay visible.
Label only the points that matter (outliers), not all of them.
recipes.combine: Add a regression line, marginal histograms or colour by a third variable.

recipes.name: Bubble chart
recipes.when: A third numeric variable is shown by size.
steps: Map the third variable to AREA, not radius: r = sqrt(v) * k, otherwise big values look far too big.
Draw the biggest bubbles first so small ones remain visible on top.
recipes.combine: Add colour for a fourth (categorical) variable.

recipes.name: Scatter-plot matrix
recipes.when: Look at every pairwise relationship in a small set of variables.
steps: A grid: cell (i, j) plots variable j (x) against variable i (y); the diagonal shows each variable's histogram.
Each variable gets its own scale, shared by its row and its column.
recipes.combine: Colour points by group; replace the upper triangle by correlation numbers (see Correlogram).

recipes.name: Correlation matrix (correlogram)
recipes.when: Which variables move together? A grid of correlation coefficients.
steps: Compute Pearson r for every pair (K.corr); the matrix is symmetric with 1 on the diagonal.
Map r from -1..1 to a diverging colour ramp (red to neutral to blue) with a neutral midpoint at 0.
Print r in each cell; use light text on dark cells.
recipes.combine: Cluster rows and columns so correlated variables sit together.

recipes.name: Connected scatter plot
recipes.when: Two variables that both change over time: see the path they take.
steps: Plot (x, y) for each period like a scatter plot, then join the points in time order.
Label start, end and a few years; arrowheads or numbers show direction.
recipes.combine: Same data as two line charts, but this shows how the relationship moves.

recipes.name: Regression line with confidence band
recipes.when: A trend plus how sure we are about it.
steps: Fit least squares with K.lin: slope b, intercept a, residual standard deviation s.
Standard error of the mean at x0: s * sqrt(1/n + (x0 - mean x)^2 / Sxx); band = fit +/- 1.99 * se (t for ~80 observations).
The band is narrowest near the mean of x and fans out at the edges: this is a polygon built from the upper and lower curves.
recipes.combine: This is a three-layer combination: points, band, line.

recipes.name: Parallel coordinates
recipes.when: Compare many numeric dimensions at once and see groups.
steps: One vertical axis per variable, each rescaled to its own min and max.
Each row becomes a polyline through its position on every axis; colour by group.
recipes.combine: Brush an axis range to highlight rows (linked views pattern).

recipes.name: Quadrant (2x2) chart
recipes.when: Prioritise items on two criteria (impact vs effort, risk vs reward).
steps: Two linear axes with the dividing lines at the midpoint (or median) of each.
Name each quadrant in its corner (high impact + low effort = "Do first", top-left here); place items as labelled dots, flipping the label to the left near the right edge.
recipes.combine: Size the dots by a third variable (becomes a bubble chart).

recipes.name: Heatmap (matrix)
recipes.when: A value for every pair of categories (hour by weekday, model by metric).
steps: Band scales on both axes; one rect per cell.
Fill with a sequential ramp (one hue, light to dark); add a thin gap so cells read as cells.
recipes.combine: Order rows and columns by similarity (clustering) to reveal blocks.

recipes.name: Radar (spider) chart
recipes.when: Profile of one or a few items across 5 to 8 comparable metrics.
steps: Axes are spokes at equal angles (2 pi / n); value maps to the distance from the centre.
Rings give the scale; connect the points of each series into a closed polygon.
Metrics must share a scale (0 to 100), otherwise the shape is meaningless.
recipes.combine: Keep to 2 or 3 series; for more, use small multiples of single radars.

recipes.name: Pie chart
recipes.when: Few parts (2 to 5) of ONE whole, where the question is "which is the biggest share?".
steps: Convert values to angles: angle = value / total * 2 pi; keep a running start angle.
Each slice is K.arc(cx, cy, 0, r, a0, a1). Start at 12 o'clock and go clockwise, largest first.
Label outside with the value; a legend is not needed with 4 slices.
recipes.combine: Use a donut with the total in the middle, or a bar chart when shares are close.

recipes.name: Donut chart
recipes.when: Same as a pie, with a total or key number in the hole.
steps: Same angles as a pie, but the inner radius is about 60% of the outer one.
The centre carries the total; this is also where a KPI value can sit.
recipes.combine: Concentric donuts (rings) compare two periods.

recipes.name: Semi-circle (half) donut
recipes.when: Parliament-style shares or a gauge-like "x of y".
steps: Use only the angles from -90 to +90 degrees (-pi/2 to pi/2).
Everything else is a normal donut: scale values to the half circle instead of the full one.
recipes.combine: Gauges (tables and dashboards family) are the same shape with one value and a needle.

recipes.name: Treemap
recipes.when: Many parts of a whole in a hierarchy; size shows the share.
steps: Sum values up the tree (K.sumTree) so every group knows its total.
Squarify the groups into the full rectangle (K.squarify keeps tiles close to squares), then squarify each group's children inside its tile.
Colour by top-level group; print labels only on tiles large enough to hold them.
recipes.combine: Click-to-zoom into a group (state = current root, then redraw) is the usual interactive extension.

recipes.name: Sunburst chart
recipes.when: A hierarchy where the path from the centre outwards matters.
steps: K.partition gives every node a fraction range [x0, x1] and a depth.
Angle = fraction * 2 pi; ring = depth. Each node is K.arc(cx, cy, ringInner, ringOuter, a0, a1).
Children inherit the colour of their top-level parent.
recipes.combine: Same data as a treemap; choose a sunburst for paths, a treemap for comparing sizes.

recipes.name: Icicle chart
recipes.when: A hierarchy as stacked rows; easier to label than a sunburst.
steps: Same K.partition layout as the sunburst, drawn as rectangles: x from x0 to x1, y from depth.
Rows are levels; width is share. Labels fit horizontally.
recipes.combine: The flame graph (flow family) is an icicle turned upside down.

recipes.name: Circle packing
recipes.when: Sizes of many items where area matters and exact position does not.
steps: Radius = sqrt(value) so AREA is proportional to value.
K.pack places circles largest first along an outward spiral at the first spot that touches no placed circle.
Centre the cloud and scale it to fit the stage.
recipes.combine: Nest packs inside bigger circles for hierarchy; colour by category.

recipes.name: Tree diagram (dendrogram layout)
recipes.when: Parent-child structure: taxonomy, file tree, clustering result.
steps: K.tree gives every node a depth (_d) and a vertical slot (_x): leaves get consecutive slots, parents sit at the middle of their children.
Map depth to x and slot to y; draw elbow links (horizontal, vertical, horizontal) before the node dots.
recipes.combine: Add leaf values as bars on the right to make a dendrogram with data.

recipes.name: Org chart
recipes.when: Reporting lines: who belongs to whom.
steps: Same K.tree layout, rotated: depth to y, slot to x.
Nodes are rounded boxes with a title; connectors drop from the parent, run sideways, then drop to each child.
recipes.combine: Colour boxes by department or add a headcount badge.

recipes.name: Nightingale rose (polar area)
recipes.when: Cyclical data (months, hours) where the circle reflects the cycle.
steps: Equal angle per category (2 pi / 12), radius = sqrt(value) so AREA, not length, encodes the value.
Draw each wedge with K.arc(cx, cy, 0, r, a0, a1); add faint rings for scale.
recipes.combine: Stack two series per wedge for a second dimension.

recipes.name: Mind map (radial tree)
recipes.when: Brainstorm structure around one central idea.
steps: Root in the centre; level-1 nodes spread around it at equal angles on a circle.
Each level-2 node sits on a larger circle within its parent's angular sector.
recipes.combine: Mermaid can generate the same from text (see the diagrams family).

recipes.name: Sankey diagram
recipes.when: Quantities moving between stages; the width of a band is the amount.
steps: Assign each node to a layer (column). A node's height = max(total in, total out) * scale.
Within a node, links stack top to bottom; each link is a cubic Bezier from the source edge to the target edge drawn with stroke-width = value * scale.
K.sankey does the layout; the recipe only draws links first (under) and nodes second.
recipes.combine: Colour links by source; highlight one path by fading the others.

recipes.name: Alluvial diagram
recipes.when: How members of categories move between categories over several time points.
steps: Same layout as a Sankey, but every column holds the same categories at a different time.
Each link is "people who were in A then and in B now"; stacking order stays consistent across columns.
recipes.combine: Add a time axis label under each column.

recipes.name: Chord diagram
recipes.when: Many-to-many relationships between a few groups (flows, co-occurrence).
steps: Each group gets an arc on the circle proportional to its total; leave a small gap between arcs.
Inside a group's arc, reserve a sub-arc for every partner, sized by the pair's value.
A ribbon joins the two sub-arcs of a pair: arc, quadratic curve through the centre, arc, quadratic back.
recipes.combine: Order groups to minimise crossing; fade all ribbons except the hovered group.

recipes.name: Arc diagram
recipes.when: Links between ordered items (chapters, timeline, genome positions).
steps: Nodes sit on one line in a meaningful order.
Each link is a half-circle above the line: radius = distance / 2, drawn with an SVG arc (A) command with sweep 1.
recipes.combine: Arc heights show distance, so sort the nodes to reveal clusters.

recipes.name: Force-directed network
recipes.when: Who is connected to whom; clusters and hubs.
steps: Give every node a random start position. For 250 steps: all pairs push apart (force k^2/d), linked pairs pull together (force d^2/k), and each node moves by that force capped by a cooling temperature (Fruchterman-Reingold).
Draw edges first, then nodes sized by degree; colour by cluster.
recipes.combine: Drag-to-pin and hover-highlight neighbours make it interactive; the same graph as a matrix is below.

recipes.name: Adjacency matrix
recipes.when: Dense networks where a node-link picture turns into a hairball.
steps: Rows and columns are the nodes (ordered by cluster so groups form blocks).
A filled cell means "these two are linked". Blocks on the diagonal reveal communities.
recipes.combine: Same data as the force network; show both side by side with linked highlighting.

recipes.name: Flame graph
recipes.when: Where time (or memory) goes in nested function calls.
steps: Build the call tree with the time spent in each node; K.sumTree adds children up.
K.partition lays every call out by its share of the total; the root sits at the bottom and callees stack upward.
Colour is decorative (warm hues). Wide boxes are the hot spots.
recipes.combine: Click a frame to zoom (make it the new root and redraw).

recipes.name: Choropleth map
recipes.when: A value per region, shown as colour (rates and ratios, not raw counts).
steps: Load a topology (world-atlas countries-110m) and convert it to GeoJSON features with topojson.feature.
A projection (d3.geoNaturalEarth1, fitted to the stage) turns lon/lat into pixels; d3.geoPath turns each feature into an SVG path string.
Look up a value per feature (here a demo value derived from the country id) and fill with a sequential ramp; add a legend bar. Antarctica is dropped so the map is not squeezed.
recipes.combine: Link it to a bar chart of the top regions, or add proportional symbols on the same projection.

recipes.name: Proportional symbol map
recipes.when: Counts or totals per place (circle area encodes the number).
steps: Draw the base map in a neutral grey so the data layer stands out.
path.centroid(feature) gives a pixel position per country; drop non-finite ones.
Radius = sqrt(value) * k. Sort so large circles are drawn first and small ones remain visible.
recipes.combine: Add a legend with 2 reference circles, or colour circles by category.

recipes.name: Dorling cartogram
recipes.when: Geography matters less than the size of the value; every region becomes a circle.
steps: Start each circle at its region centroid with area proportional to the value.
Run a few dozen relaxation passes: for every overlapping pair push the two centres apart along the line between them.
Positions stay roughly geographic, but nothing overlaps.
recipes.combine: Colour by a second variable, e.g. growth rate.

recipes.name: Tile grid map (schematic)
recipes.when: Equal visual weight for every region (small states stay visible).
steps: Hand-assign each region a (column, row) cell that roughly keeps neighbours adjacent.
Draw a square per region with its abbreviation; fill with a ramp. No projection or topology needed.
This layout is schematic, not exact geography. The values are demo values.
recipes.combine: Use it as the overview and a choropleth for detail.

recipes.name: Globe (orthographic projection)
recipes.when: Global data where distances and shapes near the poles should not be distorted.
steps: d3.geoOrthographic shows one hemisphere; rotate([lambda, phi]) decides what faces you.
Draw the sphere outline, a graticule (d3.geoGraticule10) and the countries with the same path generator.
A slider changes lambda and the whole picture is redrawn from scratch (state -> view).
recipes.combine: Add a play button that increments lambda for a spinning globe, or arcs from the flow-map recipe.

recipes.name: Flow (arc) map
recipes.when: Movement between places: routes, trade, migration.
steps: Draw the base map faded.
For each route build a GeoJSON LineString [from, to]; d3.geoPath draws it as a great-circle arc automatically.
Stroke width can encode volume; dots mark the cities.
recipes.combine: Animate dashes along the arcs or filter by origin with a dropdown (linked views).

recipes.name: Dot density map
recipes.when: Show where things are in an area without implying exact positions (one dot = N units).
steps: Zoom the projection to one region (fitSize on that feature).
Rejection sampling: draw random lon/lat inside the bounding box and keep the point only if d3.geoContains says it lies in the polygon, until you have the number of dots wanted.
Real data would sample inside sub-regions in proportion to their counts. Here the dots are random demo points.
recipes.combine: Colour dots by category for a multi-group version.

recipes.name: Contour / isoline map
recipes.when: A continuous surface (elevation, temperature, density) as filled bands.
steps: Sample the field on a grid (here a sum of Gaussian hills) into a flat array of width * height values.
d3.contours() runs marching squares at each threshold and returns polygons; scale them to pixels with d3.geoIdentity().
Fill bands from light to dark; thin lines at the thresholds act as isolines.
recipes.combine: Overlay point markers or a coastline for a real map; the same data as a heatmap is the raster version.

recipes.name: Residual plot
recipes.when: Check a regression: are errors patternless and equally spread?
steps: Fit the line (K.lin) and compute residual = observed - fitted for every point.
Plot residual (y) against fitted value (x) with a zero line. A fan shape means unequal variance, a curve means a missing non-linear term.
recipes.combine: Place beside the regression + confidence band recipe: the pair tells whether the fit can be trusted.

recipes.name: ROC curve
recipes.when: How well a score separates two classes across ALL thresholds.
steps: Sort cases by score, high to low. Sweep the threshold downwards: each case moves either true positives or false positives up by one.
Plot (false positive rate, true positive rate) after every step. The diagonal is a coin flip.
AUC = area under the curve by the trapezoid rule; 1.0 is perfect, 0.5 is chance.
recipes.combine: Draw several models as several lines; add the point for the threshold you actually use.

recipes.name: Precision-recall curve
recipes.when: Imbalanced classes, where ROC looks too optimistic.
steps: Same threshold sweep as ROC but track precision = TP / (TP + FP) and recall = TP / all positives.
The baseline is the share of positives in the data (a horizontal line), not a diagonal.
recipes.combine: Show next to ROC; report average precision (area under this curve).

recipes.name: Confusion matrix
recipes.when: What kinds of mistakes a classifier makes at one chosen threshold.
steps: Apply the threshold (score > 0.65 means "positive") and count the four outcomes: TN, FP, FN, TP.
A 2 x 2 grid, darker = more cases; print the count and the row percentage in every cell.
recipes.combine: Move the threshold with a slider and watch the ROC point move (linked views).

recipes.name: Learning curve (train vs validation loss)
recipes.when: Diagnose over- and under-fitting while a model trains.
steps: x = epoch; two lines: training loss (keeps falling) and validation loss (falls, then rises when the model overfits).
Mark the epoch with the lowest validation loss (early-stopping point) with a vertical rule.
recipes.combine: Add the learning rate schedule as a faint step line underneath (time + layering).

recipes.name: Feature importance with uncertainty
recipes.when: Which inputs a model relies on, and how stable that ranking is.
steps: For each feature take the mean importance and its standard error over repeated runs (permutation or cross-validation folds).
Sort descending, draw horizontal bars and a whisker for +/- 1.96 standard errors.
recipes.combine: Pair with partial dependence plots for the top features.

recipes.name: Partial dependence with ICE lines
recipes.when: How the prediction changes with one feature, averaged and per individual.
steps: For a grid of feature values, set that feature to each value for every row and predict (ICE = one line per row).
The thick line is the average of the ICE lines (partial dependence). Lines that cross the average in different ways reveal interactions.
recipes.combine: Stack several features as small multiples.

recipes.name: Decision boundary (k-nearest neighbours)
recipes.when: See what region of feature space a classifier assigns to each class.
steps: Two simulated classes in 2D. Build a grid of cells covering the plane.
Classify every cell centre with k = 7 nearest neighbours (vote share of class 1); colour the cell by the vote (blue to orange).
Draw the training points on top.
recipes.combine: Swap the classifier function and keep the drawing code: the pattern works for any model.

recipes.name: PCA biplot
recipes.when: Squeeze many correlated variables into 2 axes and see which variables drive them.
steps: Standardise the variables and form their correlation matrix.
Find the top two eigenvectors by power iteration (multiply a vector by the matrix until its direction stops changing), then subtract the first component and repeat.
Scores = data projected on the eigenvectors (dots); loadings = eigenvector * sqrt(eigenvalue) (arrows).
recipes.combine: Colour the dots by group or cluster; this is the basis for most "embedding scatter" plots.

recipes.name: Forest plot (meta-analysis)
recipes.when: Combine several studies: each effect with its confidence interval, plus the pooled result.
steps: One row per study: a square at the estimate (size = weight) and a line from the lower to the upper bound.

Inverse-variance pooling: each study's standard error comes from its interval, weight = 1 / se^2, pooled estimate = weighted mean, pooled se = 1 / sqrt(sum of weights). The pooled estimate is a diamond whose width is its 95% interval.
recipes.combine: Sort by year or weight; add heterogeneity statistics as text.

recipes.name: Kaplan-Meier survival curves
recipes.when: Time until an event (churn, failure, relapse) with censored observations.
steps: Sort observations by time. At each EVENT time the survival estimate is multiplied by (1 - 1/number still at risk); censored cases only reduce the risk set.
Plot the estimate as a step function starting at 1; mark censored cases with small ticks.
recipes.combine: Add confidence bands and a log-rank p-value in the corner.

recipes.name: Control chart (SPC)
recipes.when: Is a process stable, or did something change?
steps: Estimate the centre line and sigma from a baseline period (first 20 points).
Draw the centre line and the +/- 3 sigma limits; any point outside the limits is flagged.
recipes.combine: Add run rules (8 points on one side) and annotate known events.

recipes.name: Bland-Altman plot
recipes.when: Do two measurement methods agree?
steps: For every subject plot the AVERAGE of the two methods (x) against their DIFFERENCE (y).
Draw the mean difference (bias) and the limits of agreement: bias +/- 1.96 standard deviations of the differences.
recipes.combine: Pair with a scatter plot of method A vs B (which hides bias).

recipes.name: Volcano plot
recipes.when: Thousands of tests at once: effect size against significance.
steps: x = log2 fold change; y = -log10(p), so smaller p-values rise higher.
p comes from z = effect / standard error through the normal CDF; colour points that pass BOTH cut-offs (|log2FC| > 1 and p < 0.05).
recipes.combine: Label the top few genes; add a threshold line at p = 0.05.

recipes.name: Calibration (reliability) curve
recipes.when: When a model says "70%", does it happen 70% of the time?
steps: Group predictions into probability bins (0.1 wide).
For each bin plot the mean predicted probability (x) against the observed share of positives (y). The diagonal is perfect calibration.
Points below the diagonal = over-confident, above = under-confident.
recipes.combine: Show the histogram of predictions under the curve so sparse bins are not over-read.

recipes.name: Means with confidence intervals
recipes.when: Compare group averages and show the uncertainty of each.
steps: Mean per group; standard error = sd / sqrt(n); 95% interval = mean +/- 1.96 standard errors.
Dot at the mean, whisker with caps for the interval. Non-overlapping intervals suggest a real difference (overlap does not prove there is none).
recipes.combine: Overlay the raw points (jitter) so n and spread stay visible.

recipes.name: Probability shading (interactive)
recipes.when: Teach or explore p-values and tail areas of a distribution.
steps: Draw the normal density once. A slider holds the cut-off z (state).
Shade the area left of z: a path of the density from -4 to z, closed to the baseline. The probability printed is the normal CDF at z (error-function approximation).
recipes.combine: Switch to two-sided mode or overlay a second (alternative) distribution to illustrate power.

recipes.name: Function plot
recipes.when: Show curves y = f(x), their zeros and shape.
steps: Sample the function at 200 evenly spaced x values (K.range) and map each (x, f(x)) to pixels.
Draw the axes THROUGH zero (not at the border) and label x in multiples of pi.
recipes.combine: Slider for a parameter (frequency, damping) gives an interactive explorer; shade the area under a curve for integrals.

recipes.name: Parametric curve (Lissajous)
recipes.when: Curves where x and y are BOTH functions of a parameter t.
steps: Sample t from 0 to 2 pi; compute x(t) = sin(a t + delta) and y(t) = sin(b t).
Join the points in order. The ratio a : b decides the shape; delta rotates the pattern.
recipes.combine: Animate t with a Play button, or draw several (a, b) pairs as small multiples.

recipes.name: Polar plot (rose curve)
recipes.when: Quantities that depend on an angle (antenna patterns, cycles, orbits).
steps: Sample angle theta; compute radius r(theta) = cos(k theta).
Convert polar to pixels with K.polar(cx, cy, r, theta); draw rings and spokes for reference.
Negative r simply plots on the opposite side, which is what creates the petals.
recipes.combine: Overlay two patterns for comparison.

recipes.name: Ternary plot
recipes.when: Three components that sum to 100% (soil, alloys, votes in three-party races).
steps: Each point is (a, b, c) with a + b + c = 1. Place it with barycentric coordinates: x = b + c / 2, y = c * sqrt(3) / 2 inside an equilateral triangle.
Corners are 100% of one component; gridlines run parallel to the opposite side.
recipes.combine: Colour points by a fourth variable.

recipes.name: Vector field
recipes.when: A direction and magnitude at every point: flow, force, gradients.
steps: Lay a regular grid of sample points and evaluate the field (u, v) at each.
Draw a short arrow per point: direction = atan2(v, u), length proportional to magnitude (capped), colour by magnitude.
The arrowhead is a small triangle rotated by the same angle.
recipes.combine: Overlay streamlines or contour lines of the potential.

recipes.name: Phase portrait (damped pendulum)
recipes.when: Behaviour of a dynamical system: where trajectories start, spiral and settle.
steps: State = (angle, angular velocity). Equations: angle' = velocity, velocity' = -sin(angle) - 0.15 * velocity.
Integrate each starting point with 4th-order Runge-Kutta (four slope evaluations per step, 0.05 time units per step, 400 steps).
Plot the path in the (angle, velocity) plane and stop drawing when it leaves the window; all paths spiral into the stable point (0, 0).
recipes.combine: Overlay a vector field of the same equations underneath.

recipes.name: Heatmap of f(x, y)
recipes.when: A function of two variables, read as colour.
steps: Evaluate z = sin(x) cos(y) on a 40 x 28 grid.
Use a DIVERGING ramp centred on 0 so positive and negative regions are distinguishable.
recipes.combine: Add isolines (contour recipe) and a colour bar.

recipes.name: 3D surface (painter's algorithm)
recipes.when: A function of two variables as a surface, no WebGL needed.
steps: Sample z = sin(r) on a 24 x 24 grid; rotate every vertex with K.rot (two rotation matrices) and project with a simple perspective divide (K.proj).
Each grid cell is a quad. Sort quads by their average depth (far first) and draw in that order, so nearer quads cover farther ones: the painter's algorithm.
Colour by height with the diverging ramp.
recipes.combine: Add a slider for rotation (see the rotating cube) or overlay the wireframe of a second surface.

recipes.name: Mandelbrot set (escape-time fractal)
recipes.when: Illustrate iteration, complex numbers and fractals.
steps: For each pixel c = x + iy, iterate z = z^2 + c from 0. Count the steps until |z| exceeds 2 (max 30).
Points that never escape belong to the set (drawn dark); the others are coloured by how fast they escaped.
SVG draws a 64 x 40 grid of rectangles; a canvas would allow far higher resolution.
recipes.combine: Mouse drag to zoom: change the window bounds and redraw.

recipes.name: Cellular automaton (Game of Life)
recipes.when: Show emergent behaviour from simple local rules.
steps: State: a grid of booleans. One step: count the 8 neighbours (wrapping at the edges); a live cell survives with 2 or 3 neighbours, a dead cell is born with exactly 3.
Draw one rect per cell. Step button = one update then redraw; Play repeats it on a timer; clicking a cell toggles it.
recipes.combine: The same state/step/draw skeleton drives every animated explainer.

recipes.name: Signal and its spectrum (DFT)
recipes.when: See which frequencies a signal contains.
steps: Build a signal from two sine waves (3 and 9 cycles) plus noise, 64 samples.
K.dft computes the discrete Fourier transform: for every frequency k, correlate the signal with a cosine and a sine of that frequency and take the magnitude.
Top panel: the signal in time. Bottom panel: amplitude by frequency; peaks appear at 3 and 9.
recipes.combine: A spectrogram stacks many such spectra over time (time + heatmap).

recipes.name: Pendulum simulation (animation)
recipes.when: Physics you can watch: state evolves under an equation of motion.
steps: State: angle and angular velocity. Each tick advances the equation angle'' = -sin(angle) - 0.05 * angle' by two RK4 steps.
Draw: rod from the pivot to the bob, plus a fading trail of the last 60 bob positions.
Play starts a timer that calls step(); Step advances once (useful for tests and teaching).
recipes.combine: Plot the phase portrait live beside it (same state, two views).

recipes.name: Venn diagram
recipes.when: Overlaps between 2 or 3 sets.
steps: Three equal circles placed so each pair overlaps; semi-transparent fills make the intersections visible.
Print the count of each region at its centre: only-A, A and B, all three, and so on.
recipes.combine: For more than 3 sets use an UpSet-style bar chart of intersections.

recipes.name: Geometric construction
recipes.when: Illustrate a theorem or construction (circumcircle, medians, bisectors).
steps: Place triangle vertices A, B, C. Compute the circumcentre from the perpendicular-bisector formula: D = 2(ax(by - cy) + bx(cy - ay) + cx(ay - by)), then ux and uy from the squared lengths.
Draw the triangle, the circle through all three vertices (radius = distance centre to A), the centroid (mean of the vertices) and the three medians.
recipes.combine: Make the vertices draggable (pointer events + redraw) to explore.

recipes.name: Unit circle explorer (interactive)
recipes.when: Teach sine and cosine as coordinates on the unit circle.
steps: One state variable: the angle theta (a slider, 0 to 360 degrees).
Draw the circle, the radius to (cos t, sin t), the vertical segment of length sin t (orange) and the horizontal segment of length cos t (blue).
Print the numbers so the picture and the values are tied together.
recipes.combine: Plot sin and cos against theta on the right (linked views) to see the waves emerge.

recipes.name: Fourier series builder (interactive)
recipes.when: Show how simple waves add up to a complicated one.
steps: Target: a square wave. Its Fourier series is the sum of odd harmonics: sin(x) + sin(3x)/3 + sin(5x)/5 + ...
State: the number of terms n (slider). Draw the sum of the first n terms over the target.
More terms hug the target better; the overshoot at the jumps never disappears (Gibbs phenomenon).
recipes.combine: Show each term as a thin faint line and the spectrum (bars of 1/k) next to it.

recipes.name: Rotating 3D cube (no library)
recipes.when: A 3D object you can turn, without WebGL.
steps: Eight vertices at (+/-1, +/-1, +/-1); six faces as lists of four vertex indices.
Every redraw: rotate vertices (K.rot with the slider angle), project to 2D (K.proj), sort faces by average depth, draw back to front.
Flat shading: each face has its own colour; opacity gives a hint of depth.
recipes.combine: Add a 3D scatter inside the cube, or auto-rotate with a timer.

recipes.name: 3D scatter plot (rotatable)
recipes.when: Three numeric variables or three-dimensional clusters.
steps: Centre the data in a unit cube, rotate (K.rot) and project (K.proj) every point on slider change.
Size points by depth (nearer = larger) and draw far points first. Draw the cube edges as a frame.
recipes.combine: Colour by cluster; add a floor grid for orientation.

recipes.name: Particle system (animation)
recipes.when: Fountains, sparks, snow: many short-lived moving objects.
steps: State: an array of particles with position, velocity and remaining life.
Every step: spawn a few at the emitter, apply gravity to the velocity, move, reduce life, and drop the dead ones.
Opacity = remaining life, so particles fade out. Same state/step/draw skeleton as the pendulum.
recipes.combine: Add wind as a slider that changes one velocity term.

recipes.name: Declarative SVG animation (SMIL)
recipes.when: Simple loops (pulsing, travelling dots, spinning) with zero JavaScript timers.
steps: Add <animate> children that change an attribute over time (radius, opacity) with repeatCount="indefinite".
<animateMotion> moves an element along a path; <animateTransform> rotates or scales.
The browser runs it; the code only describes the loop.
recipes.combine: Use it for loading indicators or to show direction along a Sankey link or network edge.

recipes.name: Flowchart (data-driven)
recipes.when: A process with decisions.
steps: Describe the chart as DATA: nodes (id, position, size, shape, label) and edges (from, to, optional label).

One generic renderer draws every node (pill, box, diamond) and every edge: the straight line between the two centres is trimmed to the box borders (D.trim) and given an arrowhead from an SVG <marker>.
To change the chart you edit the data, never the drawing code. (Mermaid does the layout for you from text; here layout is explicit.)
recipes.combine: Add counts on the edges to turn it into a Sankey-like flow; colour nodes by status.

recipes.name: Sequence diagram
recipes.when: Who calls whom, in what order (API flows, protocols).
steps: One column per participant with a dashed lifeline. Time runs downwards.
Messages are a list [from, to, label, isReturn]; message i is drawn at y = top + i * step as a horizontal arrow between the two lifelines with its label above.
Return messages are dashed.
recipes.combine: Mermaid draws the same from text: sequenceDiagram.

recipes.name: Class diagram
recipes.when: Object-oriented design: classes, fields, methods and inheritance.
steps: Each class is a box in three compartments (name, fields, methods) separated by lines; the height comes from the number of rows.
Inheritance is a line to the parent with a hollow triangle at the parent end.
recipes.combine: Mermaid: classDiagram.

recipes.name: State machine
recipes.when: Something that is in exactly one state and moves on events (orders, connections, UI).
steps: States are rounded boxes (data: id, position); transitions are [from, to, label] edges.
Reuse the flowchart renderer, add a filled start dot and a double-ring end state.
recipes.combine: Highlight the current state and drive it from buttons (state machine + interactive).

recipes.name: Swimlane (cross-functional) diagram
recipes.when: A process that passes between people or teams.
steps: One horizontal lane per actor (band scale on y); steps are boxes placed in the lane of the actor who performs them, left to right in time order.
Arrows connect consecutive steps; a vertical segment means a hand-off.
recipes.combine: Add durations to the boxes to see where time is lost.

recipes.name: Decision tree (classifier)
recipes.when: Explain how a tree model reaches a decision.
steps: Tree data: internal nodes hold a question, leaves hold a class. K.tree gives positions (depth = row, slot = column).
Edges are labelled yes / no; leaves are coloured by class so the reader can see which regions are pure.
recipes.combine: Draw the same tree's splits as lines on a scatter plot (decision boundary recipe).

recipes.name: Network topology diagram
recipes.when: How devices and services are wired together.
steps: Hub-and-spoke layout: the router in the centre, switches on a ring around it, end devices on a larger ring around their switch.
Positions come from K.polar. Use different shapes (circle, square, hexagon) to tell device types apart, with a legend.
recipes.combine: Colour links by load to overlay data on the topology.

recipes.name: Git branch graph
recipes.when: Explain branching and merging.
steps: Each branch is a horizontal lane (y). Each commit is a circle at (x = commit index, y = its lane).
Branching: a curve from a commit on the parent lane to the first commit of the new lane; merging: a curve back. Lane colour identifies the branch.
recipes.combine: Annotate commits with tags or CI status.

recipes.name: Layered architecture diagram
recipes.when: High-level structure of a system (UI, services, data).
steps: Three full-width layers stacked top to bottom (band scale); each holds component boxes laid out evenly.
Vertical arrows show allowed calls (top layer calls the layer below).
recipes.combine: Overlay latency or error rate per component.

recipes.name: Kanban board (HTML)
recipes.when: Work items by status.
steps: Data: columns with a list of cards. HTML grid: one flex column per status.
A button on each card moves it to the next column (state change, redraw).
recipes.combine: Count per column feeds a cumulative-flow chart.

recipes.name: Sortable table
recipes.when: Rows the reader wants to rank by different columns.
steps: Keep the data in an array of row objects and a state { column, direction }.
Clicking a header sets the state and sorts a COPY of the array (numbers numerically, text alphabetically); then the whole <tbody> is rebuilt.
Align numbers right, text left; show an arrow on the sorted column.
recipes.combine: Feed the same sorted array to a chart (table and chart can never disagree).

recipes.name: Heat table (conditional formatting)
recipes.when: A table where patterns matter more than exact numbers.
steps: For every numeric column find min and max; map each cell to t = (value - min) / (max - min).
Use t as the background colour from a sequential ramp (K.seq); choose white text above t = 0.55 so contrast stays readable.
Normalise per COLUMN so different units are comparable.
recipes.combine: Add a sparkline column.

recipes.name: Table with sparklines
recipes.when: Numbers plus their recent trend in one row.
steps: Build the table rows from data; for each row add an empty cell.
Draw a tiny SVG line (K.path on the row's own series, scaled to its min and max) inside that cell.
recipes.combine: Combine with sort: re-drawing the rows keeps the sparklines aligned.

recipes.name: KPI tiles
recipes.when: The 3 to 5 numbers someone must see first.
steps: Each tile: a label, one big number, and a change versus the previous period (arrow + percent).
Colour the change by whether it is GOOD, not by whether it is positive (churn up is bad).
recipes.combine: Place above charts in a dashboard; clicking a tile filters the charts below.

recipes.name: Gauge (dial)
recipes.when: One value against a range with good/bad zones (speed, utilisation, score).
steps: Half-circle track from -90 to +90 degrees split into coloured zones with K.arc.
Needle angle = -90 + value / max * 180 degrees; draw a line from the centre with K.polar and a hub circle.
recipes.combine: Use sparingly: a bullet chart carries the same information with less space.

recipes.name: Word cloud
recipes.when: A quick look at the most frequent terms (not for precise comparison).
steps: Font size grows with the word's count (linear between 11 and 34 px).
Place words biggest first along a spiral from the centre; the first spot whose box (width = characters * size * 0.64, height = size) overlaps no placed word wins.
recipes.combine: A bar chart of the top 10 words is easier to read; use the cloud only for mood.

recipes.name: Comparison (pricing) cards
recipes.when: Two to four options compared on the same features.
steps: Data: options with a price and a feature list. One flex card per option, same feature rows in the same order.
Highlight the recommended card with a coloured border.
recipes.combine: A toggle (monthly/yearly) changes prices with one state variable.

recipes.name: Month calendar
recipes.when: Dates, deadlines and events at a glance.
steps: Find the weekday of the 1st with new Date(Date.UTC(year, month, 1)).getUTCDay() and the number of days in the month.
Fill a 7-column grid: blank cells for the offset, then one cell per day; highlight event days.
recipes.combine: Colour days by value for the calendar heatmap.

recipes.name: Searchable list (live filter)
recipes.when: Long lists where the reader knows what they are looking for.
steps: State: the search string. On every input event filter the array with a case-insensitive includes() and redraw the list.
Show the count of matches; keep the input focused (redraw only the list, not the input).
recipes.combine: Combine with a map or chart that highlights the filtered items.

recipes.name: Bubble sort stepper
recipes.when: Teach an algorithm step by step.
steps: State: the array, the position j being compared, and the number of passes done i. Step(): compare a[j] and a[j+1], swap if needed, advance j; at the end of a pass increase i.
Draw: bars; orange = being compared, green = already in final place, blue = rest.
recipes.combine: Show the comparison count as a line chart growing with n.

recipes.name: Gradient descent explorer
recipes.when: Teach learning rates: too small is slow, too large overshoots or diverges.
steps: Loss = x^2, gradient = 2x. Update: x = x - learningRate * 2x.
Slider sets the learning rate; Run repeats the update and records the trail. With rate 0.5 it lands on 0 in one step; above 1.0 it diverges.
recipes.combine: Plot loss against step number next to the parabola (linked views).

recipes.name: Binary search visualiser
recipes.when: Show why halving the search range is so fast.
steps: State: low and high indexes of the remaining range. Each step looks at the middle element and discards the half that cannot contain the target.
Draw all items as cells; dim the discarded ones; outline the current middle. 16 items need at most 4 steps.
recipes.combine: Plot steps against list size to show the logarithmic growth.

recipes.name: Compound interest calculator
recipes.when: A formula with parameters people want to play with.
steps: Inputs: start amount, yearly rate, years (sliders). Formula: balance = start * (1 + rate)^year.
Redraw a line (balance by year) with an area underneath and print the final value. Sliders are the only state.
recipes.combine: Add a second scenario line for comparison.

recipes.name: Quiz with instant feedback
recipes.when: Check understanding while reading.
steps: Data: questions with options, the index of the right option and an explanation.
Render the options as buttons; on click mark the choice right/wrong, reveal the explanation and keep a running score. Next question redraws.
recipes.combine: Log answers to build a per-topic bar chart of strengths.

recipes.name: Flashcards (flip)
recipes.when: Memorising terms and definitions.
steps: State: current card index and whether it is flipped.
Clicking the card toggles the side; Next advances the index.
recipes.combine: Track which cards were missed and show them again first (spaced repetition).

recipes.name: Countdown timer
recipes.when: Pomodoro-style focus sessions or exercises.
steps: State: seconds left and a timer handle. Every second subtract one and redraw; at zero stop.
Draw a ring whose arc length is the remaining fraction (K.arc) with the time as text in the middle.
recipes.combine: Record completed sessions and show them as a calendar heatmap.

recipes.name: UI mockup: study dashboard
recipes.when: Show what a screen could look like before building it.
steps: Layout with CSS grid: a header row, a row of metric cards (auto-fit columns so it also works on a phone), a list card.
Colours and borders come from CSS variables, so it follows light and dark mode.
Placeholder numbers only; the point is structure.
recipes.combine: Replace the placeholder numbers with real chart recipes to get a working dashboard (see "Dashboard with shared state").

recipes.name: Form with live validation
recipes.when: Collect input and tell people immediately what is wrong.
steps: One validator function per field (email shape, password length) returning an error text or an empty string.
On every input event run the validators, show the message under the field and set the submit button's disabled flag from "no errors".
Never rely on colour alone: the message text explains the problem.
recipes.combine: Add a password-strength bar drawn like a progress bar.

recipes.name: Landing page hero + feature cards
recipes.when: The top of a product or project page.
steps: A centred headline (one sentence), a sub-headline (one sentence), two buttons (primary and secondary).
Three feature cards in an auto-fit grid so they stack on small screens.
recipes.combine: Publish it as a web page (shareable link) or place real chart recipes inside the cards.

recipes.name: Poster composition
recipes.when: A single bold graphic: event poster, title slide, cover.
steps: Fix a canvas (viewBox 320 x 300) and a palette of 3 to 4 colours.
Build the layout from big simple shapes first (background, circle, bars), then the headline text with the largest size and strongest contrast, then small details (date, place).
Hierarchy: one dominant element, one secondary, the rest quiet.
recipes.combine: Use the same palette as the charts in the same document so everything looks like one family.

recipes.name: Icon set from primitives
recipes.when: Simple consistent icons without an icon font.
steps: Design on a 24 x 24 grid with one rule set: 2 px stroke, round caps and joins, no fill.
Each icon is a few primitives (circle, rect, line, path); an icon is just a function of (parent, colour).
Place them in a grid with <g transform="translate">.
recipes.combine: Use the same icons in KPI tiles and navigation.

recipes.name: Generative pattern (Truchet tiles)
recipes.when: Backgrounds and patterns from a tiny rule plus randomness.
steps: Divide the area into square tiles. Each tile gets one of two orientations at random (seeded, so the picture is reproducible).

Orientation 0 draws two quarter-circle arcs around the top-left and bottom-right corners; orientation 1 around the other two. The arcs always meet the neighbours' arcs at edge midpoints, which creates the flowing lines.
recipes.combine: Colour the arcs by a data value to make a "data texture".

recipes.name: Flow field art
recipes.when: Organic, wind-like line art driven by a vector field.
steps: Define an angle at every point: angle(x, y) = (sin(x * 0.02) + cos(y * 0.025)) * pi.
Start many curves at jittered grid points and take 40 small steps, each in the direction of the local angle.
Draw each trail as a thin semi-transparent path; colour by index.
recipes.combine: The same loop traces streamlines of a real vector field (physics recipe).

recipes.name: Mandala (rotational symmetry)
recipes.when: Decorative radial designs.
steps: Draw ONE petal as a path with two quadratic curves (centre, control point left, tip, control point right, back to centre).
Repeat it n times, each rotated by 360 / n degrees; stack layers with different n, length and colour.
recipes.combine: Map a data series to petal length to make a radial bar chart with style.

recipes.name: Isometric blocks
recipes.when: 3D-looking bars, buildings or city skylines without a 3D engine.
steps: Isometric projection of grid cell (i, j): x = (i - j) * w, y = (i + j) * w / 2; height lifts a block by subtracting from y.
A block is three polygons in the same colour: top as is, left side with a 22% black overlay, right side with 42%, which fakes lighting. Opaque faces plus back-to-front order hide what is behind.
Draw back to front (increasing i + j).
recipes.combine: Block height = data value gives an isometric bar chart over a map grid.

recipes.name: Pixel art from a text map
recipes.when: Sprites, tiny icons, retro graphics.
steps: Describe the image as an array of strings: one character per pixel, "." for empty.
Loop over rows and characters; each non-empty character becomes a square coloured from a small palette object.
recipes.combine: Animate by swapping two frames of the map every half second.

recipes.name: Flat illustration: sunset over hills
recipes.when: Decorative scenes and hero images.
steps: Paint back to front: sky bands, sun (two circles), distant birds, then three overlapping hill paths from light to dark.
Hills are single paths using Q (quadratic) curves closed along the bottom edge.
Limit the palette to about eight colours so it reads as one picture.
recipes.combine: Use as a background layer behind a chart or title.

recipes.name: Dashboard with shared state (KPIs + chart + table)
recipes.when: Several views of the same data that must always agree.
steps: ONE data array and ONE state object ({ region }). Every view is a function render(rows) of the filtered rows.
A select changes the state and calls update(), which recomputes the filtered rows once and re-renders the KPI tiles, the bar chart and the table from them.
Because all three read the same rows, a number in a tile can never differ from the chart.
recipes.combine: This is the general recipe for dashboards: add a view = add one render function.

recipes.name: Annotated line chart (event band + callout)
recipes.when: Tell the story: what happened when.
steps: Draw the data layer first (line).

Add an annotation layer in the SAME coordinates: a shaded rect for a period (x from the start month to the end month), a vertical dashed rule for an event, and a callout (leader line + text) at the peak.
Annotations go behind the line (band) or beside it (callout) so they never hide data.
recipes.combine: Any chart can take this layer: it is just extra marks that use the chart's scales.

recipes.name: Linked map + bar chart (click to select)
recipes.when: Geography and ranking together, each explaining the other.
steps: One state: the set of selected regions. Both views are redrawn from (values, selection).
Clicking a tile or a bar toggles that region in the set; selected regions are orange in BOTH views, others blue.
The two views share the colour logic through one function: colourOf(region).
recipes.combine: Use a real choropleth instead of tiles, or add a table.

recipes.name: Sortable table + bar chart that stay in sync
recipes.when: Readers want both the exact numbers and the picture, ordered the same way.
steps: One array of rows and one sort state. A single draw() sorts a copy of the rows and builds BOTH the table and the bars from that sorted copy.
Clicking a header changes the state and calls draw(), so the two always have the same order.
recipes.combine: Add a filter input (see Searchable list) to the same draw().

recipes.name: Small multiples of lines with a shared scale
recipes.when: Compare many time series at a glance.
steps: Compute the y range ONCE over all series (shared scale) so a taller line really means a bigger value.
Lay panels on a grid; each panel is the same line-chart code with its own title and a dot on the last value.
recipes.combine: Highlight the panel that deviates most, or sort panels by slope.

recipes.name: Rotating 3D solids you can turn with the mouse
recipes.when: Look at a 3D object from every side without WebGL: cube, torus, sphere, Mobius strip.
steps: A mesh is just data: a list of vertices [x, y, z] and a list of faces (indexes of 3 or 4 vertices). Short functions generate them: cube (8 vertices), torus (a u x v grid wrapped around), icosphere (an icosahedron whose triangles are split twice and pushed onto a sphere), Mobius strip (a strip whose width direction flips half-way round).
Every frame: rotate each vertex (V.rot, two angles), project it (V.proj: perspective divide f = d / (d - z), so nearer points get bigger).

Lighting: for each face compute the normal with a cross product, flip it to face the camera (two-sided lighting, needed for the one-sided Mobius strip) and take its dot product with a light direction. Brightness = 22% + 48% * that value.
Painter's algorithm: sort faces by mean depth, far to near, and fill them in that order so near faces cover far ones.
Interaction: dragging changes the two view angles (V.drag); the Spin button adds 0.7 radians per second to the y angle inside the loop; Wireframe skips the fill.
recipes.combine: Colour faces by a data value, draw a 3D scatter inside the same scene, or animate the vertices (see the wave surface).

recipes.name: Solar system (orbits in 3D, drag to tilt)
recipes.when: Show motion that depends on distance, in a scene you can view from any angle.
steps: Each planet has an orbit radius r and an angular speed from Kepler's third law: period ~ r^1.5, so speed ~ r^-1.5 (inner planets are much faster).
Every frame the clock t advances by dt * speed (slider). A planet's 3D position is [r cos(w t), 0, r sin(w t)]; the Moon is the Earth's position plus a small fast orbit.
Orbits are polylines of 90 points; everything goes through the same rotate + project functions, so dragging tilts the whole system.
Drawing order: collect the sun, planets and moon with their depth, sort by depth, draw far to near. Circle size = base size * perspective factor, so nearer planets look bigger.
recipes.combine: Add a trail per planet (keep the last positions, draw them fading), or plot distance-to-sun against time in a linked line chart.

recipes.name: Lorenz attractor (a 3D curve being drawn live)
recipes.when: Show chaos: a deterministic system whose path never repeats and never settles.
steps: Three coupled equations: dx = sigma (y - x), dy = x (rho - z) - y, dz = x y - beta z, with sigma = 10, beta = 8/3 and rho from the slider (28 gives the butterfly).
Integrate with 4th-order Runge-Kutta: evaluate the slope four times per step and average (more accurate than plain Euler). 6 steps of dt = 0.01 per frame.

Keep the last 2500 points. Every frame rotate and project them all and draw them in chunks of 40 points, each chunk with its own colour (old = blue, new = orange) and a line width that grows with perspective.
The view rotates slowly by itself; drag to take over. Changing rho resets the trail so you see how the shape changes (below about 24.7 it settles to a point instead of being chaotic).
recipes.combine: Run a second copy from a start point that differs by 0.001 and draw both: they separate, which is sensitive dependence on initial conditions (see the double pendulum).

recipes.name: Starfield fly-through (steer with the pointer)
recipes.when: A cheap sense of depth and speed: points rushing past the camera.
steps: Each star has a fixed (x, y) and a depth z that shrinks every frame (z -= speed * dt). When z reaches almost 0 the star is respawned far away at z = 1.
Perspective projection by hand: screen = centre + (x / z) * focal length; stars close to the camera fly outwards fast.
Draw each star as a short line from its previous screen position to the new one (a streak) and make it bigger and brighter as z falls.
Steering: the pointer position moves the vanishing point (the centre everything flies away from).
recipes.combine: Colour the stars by a data category and you have a 3D scatter you fly through.

recipes.name: Animated 3D wave surface
recipes.when: A surface that changes over time: ripples, heat, a height field of data.
steps: A height field: a 26 x 26 grid of (x, z) points whose height is y = 0.28 sin(3 r - 2 t) / (1 + 1.5 r), with r the distance from the centre and t the clock. The ripple moves outwards as t grows.
Every frame recompute all y values for the current t, rotate, project and sort the 625 quads by depth (painter's algorithm), then fill each with a colour from its mean height.
The view turns slowly by itself and can be dragged.
recipes.combine: Replace the formula by a grid of real measurements per time step to animate a real field, e.g. temperature.

recipes.name: Double pendulum (chaos: two almost identical starts)
recipes.when: Show sensitive dependence on initial conditions: tiny differences grow until the motions look unrelated.
steps: State: two angles and two angular velocities. The equations of motion (equal masses and lengths) give the two angular accelerations from the current state; integrate with RK4 (4 slope evaluations per step), 4 steps of dt = 0.01 per frame.
Two pendulums start with angles that differ by 0.001 rad. They look identical for a few seconds, then separate completely.
Draw rods, bobs and a fading trail of the lower bob of each (last 220 positions).
recipes.combine: Plot the distance between the two bobs over time to see the exponential separation (linked line chart).
